s1.syndrome_frame: A patient with a history of type 2 diabetes and hypertension presents with symptoms of fatigue, light-headedness, and dyspnea on exertion, and has abnormal heart rhythm and conduction
salient_findings: Abnormal heart rhythm with prolonged PR interval and right bundle-branch block
key_facts: Patient is in their 70s
Medical history of type 2 diabetes
Medical history of hypertension
Presenting symptoms of fatigue, light-headedness, and dyspnea on exertion
Heart rate of 47 beats per minute
Blood pressure of 148/59 mm Hg
ECG findings of normal sinus rhythm with prolonged PR interval and right bundle-branch block
Some P waves do not conduct to ventricles
Prolonged His-ventricular interval of 75 milliseconds on first conducted beat, extending to 277 milliseconds on second conducted beat
Normal biventricular function on echocardiogram
No significant valvular lesions on echocardiogram

raw.syndrome_frame: A patient with a history of type 2 diabetes and hypertension presents with symptoms of fatigue, light-headedness, and dyspnea on exertion, and has abnormal heart rhythm and conduction

shortlist.label: Mobitz Type II Atrioventricular Block
shortlist.why_kept: Prolonged PR interval and some P waves do not conduct to ventricles

shortlist.label: Third-Degree Atrioventricular Block
shortlist.why_kept: Prolonged His-ventricular interval and abnormal heart rhythm

shortlist.label: Sick Sinus Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Abnormal heart rhythm and conduction with fatigue and light-headedness

shortlist.label: Bifascicular Block
shortlist.why_kept: Right bundle-branch block and prolonged PR interval

shortlist.label: Trifascicular Block
shortlist.why_kept: Prolonged His-ventricular interval and abnormal heart conduction

raw.rationale: The patient's ECG findings of a prolonged PR interval, right bundle-branch block, and some P waves not conducting to ventricles, along with the electrophysiology study showing a prolonged His-ventricular interval, are consistent with trifascicular block, which involves dysfunction of all three fascicles of the cardiac conduction system.

rejected.label: Mobitz Type II Atrioventricular Block
rejected.why: While the patient has some P waves not conducting to ventricles, the presence of a prolonged PR interval and right bundle-branch block suggests a more complex conduction abnormality than Mobitz Type II.

rejected.label: Third-Degree Atrioventricular Block
rejected.why: There is no complete block of atrioventricular conduction, as evidenced by the presence of conducted beats with a prolonged PR interval.

rejected.label: Sick Sinus Syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's sinus rhythm is normal, and there is no evidence of sinoatrial node dysfunction.

rejected.label: Bifascicular Block
rejected.why: The presence of a prolonged His-ventricular interval suggests involvement of the His-Purkinje system, which is not limited to two fascicles.
